title: Force, Mass and Acceleration in One Dimension
learningObjectives: Describe how a constant net force changes velocity over time when mass is constant
Explain that acceleration is directly proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass
Identify that zero net force means constant velocity and no acceleration

sources.title: Newton's Laws of Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

explanations.text: An object keeps its state of motion when the net force is zero, so it maintains a constant velocity along a straight line until an unbalanced force acts.

evidence.quote: An object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed and in a straight line
If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.

explanations.text: When mass is constant, the net force determines acceleration through the relationship force equals mass times acceleration, so larger force gives larger acceleration for the same mass.

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

explanations.text: For a given net force, a more massive object accelerates less because acceleration is inversely proportional to mass.

evidence.quote: The amount of acceleration is also inversely proportional to the mass of the object
